q: The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree is called the ____ (or) heat capacity of the object.
e: Heat capacity is the heat to raise the whole sample by 1 K, C = Q/Δθ. The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree is called the thermal capacity (or) heat capacity of the object.

q: The thermal capacity of an object is given by the formula $C =$ ____.
e: The thermal capacity of an object is given by the formula C = (ΔQ)/(ΔT). Leave the relation as (ΔQ)/(ΔT).

q: In SI unit, the unit of thermal capacity is ____ ($J K^{-1}$).
e: In SI unit, the unit of thermal capacity is joule per kelvin (J K^-1). The unit written here is joule per kelvin.

q: The thermal capacity of an object depends on ____ and a type of the material it is made of.
e: The thermal capacity of an object depends on mass and a type of the material it is made of. Mass is what this statement is using.

q: Water has a relatively ____ thermal capacity.
e: Water has a relatively high thermal capacity. High is what this statement is using.

q: Because of high thermal capacity, water is used to ____ engines.
e: Because of high thermal capacity, water is used to cool engines. Cool is what this statement is using.

q: Suppose that the internal energy of ____ of a substance changes by $\Delta Q$ due to the temperature change $\Delta T$.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. Suppose that the internal energy of n moles of a substance changes by ΔQ due to the temperature change ΔT.

q: The thermal capacity for 1 mole is ____.
e: The thermal capacity for 1 mole is molar thermal capacity. Molar thermal capacity is what this statement is using.

q: SI units of the molar thermal capacity is ____ ($J mol^{-1}K^{-1}$).
e: SI units of the molar thermal capacity is joule per mole per kelvin (J mol^-1K^-1). The unit written here is joule per mole per kelvin.
